findings: The gap is a cliff at >= 40 connections / >= 100 crossings; at 10M work the strict first pass plus reachability floods use the whole budget and negotiation never starts.
At 200M work (single variant) the 24 srj19 gap boards reach 95.7 % of connections and 6 are clean; most failures then are 'ripped up and not routed again' and rip-cap rejections.
Fast bends (approximate bend costs) give +4 pts routed and 0 -> 12 % clean at equal wall time; rip limit 40 + 40 passes: 33 % -> 54 % clean at 50M on the gap boards.
tscircuit's solutions used as hard/soft guides did not help: topology alone is not the missing piece; the lattice cannot reproduce its off-grid geometry.
Deep-ring-first and longest-first orders, global router corridors, a coarser/finer lattice and negotiating from the first pass all lose at equal work.
GPU fields give the identical result 1.7x faster on one board, but slower with 12 boards in parallel (contention).
